title: Inference-Time Scaling of Diffusion Models via Progressive Seed Pruning
summary: This paper proposes a method for scaling diffusion models at inference time using progressive seed pruning, which reduces the computational cost of seed search. The approach is shown to be effective in improving the efficiency of diffusion models.
why_builders_care: Builders can use this method to optimize the performance of their diffusion models, reducing the computational cost and improving the overall efficiency of their AI systems.

title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
summary: This paper introduces MIRROR, a framework for multi-modal reasoning that learns from different views of the same data. The approach is shown to be effective in improving the performance of vision-language models.
why_builders_care: Builders can use MIRROR to develop more effective multi-modal models that can reason about different types of data, such as images and text.

title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
summary: This paper proposes X$^3$-OPD, a method for distilling reasoning into large audio-language models using on-policy alignment. The approach is shown to be effective in improving the performance of audio-language models.
why_builders_care: Builders can use X$^3$-OPD to develop more effective audio-language models that can reason about audio and text data.

title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
summary: This paper introduces DONDO, a set of open-source speech-recognition base models for African languages. The models are shown to be effective in improving the performance of speech recognition systems for African languages.
why_builders_care: Builders can use DONDO to develop more effective speech recognition systems for African languages, which can be used in a variety of applications such as voice assistants and language translation.

title: livetennisapi/livetennisapi-mcp
summary: This repository provides an MCP server for the Live Tennis API, which allows AI agents to access real-time tennis scores, odds, and model win-probability.
why_builders_care: Builders can use this repository to develop AI agents that can access real-time tennis data and make predictions about match outcomes.

title: GPT-Red: Unlocking Self-Improvement for Robustness
summary: This blog post introduces GPT-Red, a system for self-improvement of language models that uses self-play to improve AI safety, alignment, and prompt injection robustness.
why_builders_care: Builders can use GPT-Red to develop more robust and safe language models that can be used in a variety of applications such as chatbots and language translation.

title: OptiMCP
summary: This repository provides OptiMCP, a tool for verifying the math and logic of AI agents against a set of rules.
why_builders_care: Builders can use OptiMCP to ensure that their AI agents are functioning correctly and making accurate predictions.

summary: This blog post introduces Nativ, a tool for running AI models locally on a Mac.
why_builders_care: Builders can use Nativ to develop and test AI models on their local machines, which can be more convenient and efficient than using cloud-based services.
